decisions.reason: The same-message MODIFY already records that the second V is locked and must remain unchanged unless the client explicitly requests a change.
The Hero V was already approved and locked, and its same-message MODIFY fully adds the requirement to carry it forward unchanged unless the client explicitly requests a change.
The same-message MODIFY already requires complete-wordmark exploration to occur around the locked Hero V, second V, and É accent.
The existing same-message MODIFY already confines letterform exploration to the area around the three locked assets while requiring those assets to remain unchanged.

Locking the approved É accent does not itself change the candidate's terminal construction or shared-terminal attributes; any earlier inconsistency concerning the second V is not newly entailed by this source decision.
The asset-lock decision does not change the deferred champagne-metal material treatment, its qualities, or its application sequence.
Locking the three signature assets does not alter the broader brand-purpose, emotional-expression, or luxury-positioning requirements.
The decision to lock the É accent and both Vs leaves unchanged the requirement for a proprietary wordmark-led identity without a separate icon or monogram.
The source decision governs revision of wordmark elements and does not change the final production-ready asset deliverable.
